# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene + tool-timeout plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together.   e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters

  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool

  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity

  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user

  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client

pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src

pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.
4	
5	## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius
6	
7	**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.
8	
9	## Repository layout
10	
11	```
12	vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
13	packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
14	  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
15	  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
...
26	  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
27	  context/     request-context plugins
28	  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
29	  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
30	  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
31	  todo/        todo_write tool
32	  plan/        plan mode as logged state
33	  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
34	  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
35	  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
36	  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
37	  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
38	  identity/    anonymous identity
39	  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
40	  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
41	  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
42	  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
...
47	  util/        zero-dependency utilities
48	python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
49	native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
50	examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
51	.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
52	docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
53	scripts/     repo gates and generators
54	website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
55	data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
56	```
57	
58	Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).
59	
60	## Commands
61	
62	```sh
63	pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
64	pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
65	pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
66	pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
67	pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
68	pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
69	pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
70	pnpm run typecheck
71	pnpm run lint
72	pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
73	pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
74	pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
75	pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
76	pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
77	pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
78	pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
79	pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
80	pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
81	```
82	
83	### Host sandbox failures
84	
85	When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.
86	
87	### Run relevant checks locally
88	
89	Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.
90	
91	- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
92	- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
93	- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).
94	
95	## Secrets / .env
96	
97	Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.
98	
99	## Conventions
100	
...
137	Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.
138	
139	Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.
140	
141	Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.
142	
143	## Editing these instructions
144	
145	`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when required content genuinely needs the space.
146	
147	## Vendoring policy
148

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	A frozen, paired, budgeted comparison of two arms. A plan names the environments, the repetition count, and the two arms — each a model route and who implements its cells; a content digest freezes it before any cell runs; both arms run through `ctx.fleet` at the same repetition indexes under stamp groups derived from that digest; and the paired certificate-rate delta comes back with a bootstrap confidence interval, the caps both arms ran under, and a `promote` / `reject` / `inconclusive` verdict. Nothing here calls a model. The [experiments](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-experiments.md) and [budget-parity](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-08-budget-parity-for-delegated-cells.md) Agent Notes own the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: environments
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments'
12	- id: environment-runner
13	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner'
14	  config:
15	    isolation: none
16	- id: fleet
17	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fleet'
18	  config:
19	    maxConcurrent: 4
20	- id: experiments
21	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments'
22	  config:
23	    bootstrapResamples: 2000
24	    confidenceLevel: 0.95
25	    minimumDelta: 0.05
26	    cellTokenCap: 200000
27	    tokenBudget: 20000000
28	```
29	
30	| Key | Default | Meaning |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| `bootstrapResamples` | `1000` | Resamples drawn per interval. Below convergence the interval still moves with the digest; raising it narrows that movement at linear cost. |
33	| `confidenceLevel` | `0.95` | Coverage of every reported interval. |
34	| `minimumDelta` | `0` | Certificate-rate delta the overall interval's lower bound must exceed to promote. |
35	| `cellTokenCap` | none | Tokens one cell may spend. Required: it is what the plan's projection multiplies. |
36	| `tokenBudget` | none | Tokens one plan's projection may reach. Required: a plan projecting more is refused before it starts. |
37	
38	The service requires `environments` and `fleet`. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step; it returns the four `thresholds` the plan digest freezes beside the `tokenBudget`, which stays outside the digest because it bounds what a deployment pays for rather than what the comparison measures.
39	
40	## Service contract
41	
42	`ctx.experiments.run(plan)` takes `environments` (registered ids, each named once), a positive integer `repetitions`, the `baseline` and `candidate` arms, an existing absolute `workspaceRoot`, and optionally a `policyVersion` both arms' routes serve, a base `seed`, a `digest` the caller froze earlier, a `signal`, and a `sink`.
43	
44	Each arm is a model route — `provider` and `model` — its first attempt runs on, an optional `ladder` of one rung per attempt, and an optional `implementer`, the same values a fleet plan takes: `{ kind: 'route' }`, which an arm naming none runs, has every attempt of every cell of that arm driven on the arm's own route, while `{ kind: 'subagent', provider, label? }` delegates each attempt to that registered subagent provider. The [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-two-implementers) owns what a delegated certificate proves and which providers an isolation claim above `none` refuses.
45	
46	Both arms' implementers are checked at freeze, through `ctx.environmentRuns.checkImplementer` against each arm's own route, and the runner's `EnvironmentRunError` propagates unchanged. It is what keeps "every refusal happens before the first cell runs" true of a provider the composition cannot honor: the arms run as one batch, so a candidate arm whose provider is missing would otherwise spend the baseline arm's cells beside its own failing ones and then leave every repetition unpaired for a verdict of `inconclusive`.
47	
48	Both arms' model routes are checked for the same reason and with the same effect, by [the fleet](../fleet/README.md#service-contract) as it prepares the two plans of the paired run — after the freeze, still before either arm's first cell — so an arm on a route the composition does not hold, or one whose credential reference resolves to nothing, refuses the experiment rather than half-spending it. That `LlmError` propagates unchanged too.
49	
50	An arm's `ladder` is the same list a fleet plan takes and rides through to every cell of that arm, and its first rung is the arm's own route: it either names no model, or names exactly the arm's `provider` and `model`. A first rung naming another route is refused with `EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT`, because the arm is what the result and every scoreboard row are published under and a first attempt on another route would publish that identity over a route it never ran. The rest of the rungs are free, which is what a cheap-then-strong or a downshift arm is.
51	
52	It rejects with `ExperimentError` before running any cell: `EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN` for a non-positive or fractional `repetitions`, a `seed` that is not a safe non-negative integer, an empty environment list, an arm ladder with no rung, an id named twice, or an id the registry does not hold; `EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT` when an arm's first rung names a route other than the arm's own; `EXPERIMENT_UNEQUAL_CAPS` when the two arms would run their cells under different caps; `EXPERIMENT_PLAN_NOT_FROZEN` when a declared `digest` differs from the recomputed one; `EXPERIMENT_OVER_BUDGET` when `environments × repetitions × 2 × cellTokenCap` exceeds `tokenBudget`.
53	
54	Both arms are forwarded the same `policyVersion` and the same base `seed`, and each arm's cell samples with `seed + repetition`, so the paired repetitions of the two arms differ only in the arm itself, its route and its implementer — the [fleet README](../fleet/README.md#policy-version-and-the-base-seed) owns the arithmetic and the [runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#sampling-and-what-a-replay-reproduces) what a replay reproduces.
55	
56	Both arms then run as one `ctx.fleet.runPaired` call over the same ids at the same repetition count, each carrying its own arm's route and implementer. The fleet interleaves the two arms' cells — the baseline cell of one environment and repetition beside the candidate cell of the same one, then the next repetition, then the next environment — so an arm is not confounded with the hour it ran in, a provider-side drift between the arms lands on both, and each arm still comes back as the report its own plan would have produced alone. A cell the fleet kept as an error leaves its repetition unpaired rather than failing the experiment, and the result lists it under `errors` with its arm, environment, repetition, and the fleet's code and message, so a stored result says why a repetition did not pair without the process that ran it. The result is written to `sink` as one JSON line and the sink is closed exactly once; the sink is the trajectory exporter's `TrajectorySink`, so `jsonlFileSink(path)` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories` serves both exports.
57	
58	The result restates each arm beside its stamp group: `arms.baseline` and `arms.candidate` carry the `model` route, the `ladder` the arm escalated over when it named one, and the `implementer` the arm ran under, with an omitted implementer stated as `{ kind: 'route' }`, so a stored result tells a harness-native arm from a delegated one without the plan that produced it. `caps` states the ceilings every cell of both arms ran under, in cap evaluation order, so a reader of a stored result sees the budget the comparison was measured inside without finding the composition behind it.
59	
60	### The arms run under one budget
61	
62	A cell stopped at one wall or token ceiling measures something different from the same cell stopped at another, so two arms bounded differently compare the ceilings as much as the arms. `ctx.environmentRuns.cellCaps` answers what one cell of an arm runs under — [the runner README](../environment-runner/README.md#the-budget-a-delegated-attempt-runs-under) owns how a delegated cell is bounded and which cap it can lose — and a plan whose two arms resolve to different lists is refused with `EXPERIMENT_UNEQUAL_CAPS` before either arm starts. The refusal spends nothing, which is the point: the arms would otherwise run in full to produce a comparison a reader must then discount.
63	
64	`foldExperiment(request)` is the pure fold behind the run and is exported for tests and offline tools, together with `planDigest`, `capsAgree`, `describeCaps`, `experimentGroup`, `ladderConflicts`, `parseExperimentGroup`, `projectedTokens`, `EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES`, `EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX`, and the `bootstrapIntervals` pass.
65	
66	## Freezing and the group scheme
67	
68	`planDigest(plan, thresholds, caps)` is the SHA-256 hex digest over a format version, the two arms in role order — each its model route, its implementer, and its attempt ladder — the environment ids **sorted**, the repetition count, the `policyVersion` and base `seed`, the four thresholds, and the caps both arms agreed on. Sorting makes the digest independent of the order a caller listed the ids in; the workspace root, the abort signal, and the sink are not digested because they change nothing the comparison measures. The policy version and the seed are digested because both arms' sessions are found in the logs by the groups the digest mints, so two comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group. The caps are digested because they decide when a cell stops; the deployment's `tokenBudget` stays outside, because it bounds what a deployment pays for across plans rather than what one comparison measures.
69	
70	An arm's implementer enters the digest as the default `{ kind: 'route' }` when the arm names none, so a plan that omits the field and one that spells it out are one experiment; a delegated arm digests its subagent provider and label, in fixed positions that the key order a caller wrote cannot change. Which arm delegates is part of the identity, because the roles are digested in order. An arm's ladder digests one entry per rung, with `null` for a rung that names no model, so two arms that escalate differently are two experiments while a plan that ladders nothing digests as it always did.
71	
72	Each arm runs under the stamp `group` `experiment-<digest>-baseline` or `experiment-<digest>-candidate`, which the environment runner writes into the `environment/run` event of every session of that arm before its first turn. That group is the durable link from a result back to its sessions: `ctx.scorekeeper.leaderboard({ group })` selects one arm out of every persisted log, and the trajectory export carries the same string. The `experiment-` prefix is this package's reserved namespace, and the package invariant rejects a stamp that claims it without a 64-hex digest and a known arm role.
73	
74	## Statistics and verdict
75	
76	A repetition pairs when both arms reported it. Per environment the result states `pairs`, `unpaired`, the `baselineRate` and `candidateRate` over the paired repetitions, their `delta`, the mean `attemptsDelta`, and the summed `inputTokenDelta` and `outputTokenDelta`; the overall `delta` is the mean over every paired repetition of every environment.
77	
78	Each interval is a percentile bootstrap over the paired deltas: a resample draws, within every environment, as many paired deltas as that environment holds, with replacement, and the overall statistic of a resample is the mean over every drawn delta, so an environment weighs by its paired count and an environment with no pair contributes nothing rather than a zero. Every draw comes from a mulberry32 generator seeded with the 32-bit FNV-1a hash of `<digest>:<environmentId>`, so the same frozen plan over the same certificates replays to the same interval in any process; a fold with no pair at all reports no interval.
79	
80	The verdict reads the overall interval: `promote` when its lower bound exceeds `minimumDelta`, `reject` when its upper bound is below zero, `inconclusive` otherwise — including when nothing paired. `promote` is tested first, so a negative `minimumDelta` still promotes rather than producing an order-dependent answer.
81	
82	## Model Experience
83	
84	None, as an experiment schedules fleet runs and folds their reports; the environment runner owns every model-visible effect of each cell.
85	
86	#### KV Cache effect
87	
88	None; the service neither adds to nor changes any model request.
89	
90	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
91	
92	- **A preset cannot be an arm** — an arm names a model route and an implementer, and `EnvironmentRunRequest` carries no agent preset, so two compositions over one route stay incomparable until the runner and the fleet cell carry one; the plan gains an optional preset per arm with that field, never before.
93	- **A delegated arm's tokens are the child's own accounting** — an external implementer spends in another product, so a delegated cell's `usage` is what each child reported (or, for an in-process child, what this process summed for it), as [the runner](../environment-runner/README.md#the-two-implementers) records it on `environment/delegation`: the `spend` and the token deltas compare a product's published counts with a harness log's, the projection still reserves `cellTokenCap` for every cell of both arms, and a child whose backend publishes no usage leaves its cell without any.
94	- **Paired repetition indexes are not paired seeds** — the `environment/run` stamp carries no seed, so pairing removes environment variance but not run-to-run variance.
95	- **The plan's token budget is projected, not enforced** — the refusal multiplies `cellTokenCap` by the cell count, while what a cell actually spends is capped by [the budget policy](../../guard/budget-policy/README.md) whose caps `caps` states. The two are independent numbers: nothing writes a plan's `cellTokenCap` into the per-cell policy, so a plan can project less than its cells are allowed to spend.
96	- **The digest freezes the plan, not the world** — the harness commit, the environment content hashes, and the provider's model version behind a route are outside it, so two runs of one digest are comparable only under an unchanged harness and registry.
97	- **No staged evaluation and no archive** — one plan runs one stage; the staged evaluation ladder, the variant archive, and cells derived from diagnosis evidence are named by the [four-goal-workflows note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) and live outside this package.
98

1	/**
2	 * Pure types of the environment runner: the run request, the implementer that
3	 * does its work, the durable record of one delegated attempt, and the run
4	 * report, free of host-side imports.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types
7	 */
8	
9	import type { BudgetCap } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
10	import type { EnvironmentId, EnvironmentRunModel, EnvironmentRunStamp } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environments/types'
11	import type { TokenUsage } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
12	import type { SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
13	import type { SubagentStopReason } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subagent'
14	import type { CheckResult, VerificationCertificate } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/types'
15	
16	declare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/types' {
17	  interface SessionEventMap {
18	    /**
19	     * One attempt of a delegated cell, appended after the child run settled
20	     * and before the runner validates the tree it left: which provider ran it,
21	     * the run's parent-scoped id, how it ended, the structured result it
22	     * returned, the model usage this process can account for, and the model and
23	     * spend the child's own backend reported. Log-only — it never enters model
24	     * history, and it is the cell session's only record of an implementer whose
25	     * own transcript stays in its product.
26	     *
27	     * The model the cell ASKED for is on the `environment/run` stamp — its
28	     * `ladder` rung for this attempt, or its `model` for a run without one —
29	     * which the runner also passes to the provider, so a reader comparing the
30	     * two sees whether the child ran the arm's model and which concrete version
31	     * an alias resolved to.
32	     */
33	    'environment/delegation': EnvironmentDelegation
34	  }
35	}
36	
37	/**
38	 * Who implements the work of one run: the session's own model route, driven
39	 * turn by turn as the runner has always driven it, or one out-of-band coding
40	 * agent started per attempt through the subagent seam.
41	 */
42	export type EnvironmentRunImplementer =
43	  | { readonly kind: 'route' }
44	  | {
45	    readonly kind: 'subagent'
46	    /** Registered `ctx.subagents` provider each attempt's child run starts on. */
47	    readonly provider: string
48	    /** Short display label persisted with a session-backed child; absent leaves the provider's own naming. */
49	    readonly label?: string
50	  }
51	
52	/**
53	 * What one implementer carries from an attempt into the next one. A route
54	 * implementer works in the cell session itself, so every later attempt reads
55	 * the whole transcript of the earlier ones (`kept`); a subagent implementer
56	 * runs one fresh child per attempt, which starts from the text it is given and
57	 * nothing else (`dropped`). The two therefore measure different instruments on
58	 * the same ladder, which is why every attempt states which it ran under.
59	 */
60	export type EnvironmentRunTranscript = 'kept' | 'dropped'
61	
62	/**
63	 * How one delegated attempt ended: in the subagent seam's terminal vocabulary
64	 * when the child settled on its own, or `budget-deadline` when the wall budget
65	 * the attempt ran under ran out first.
66	 *
67	 * The runner cancels a child at that deadline, so the seam would report the
68	 * cancellation as its own `aborted`. Recording it apart is what lets a reader
69	 * tell an operator's cancellation from an attempt that ran out of the wall
70	 * budget its arm was measured under; a `budget-deadline` attempt is always
71	 * followed by the `budget/breach` it caused, whose scope says whether the cell
72	 * ended with it or the run moved to the next rung.
73	 */
74	export type EnvironmentDelegationStopReason = SubagentStopReason | 'budget-deadline'
75	
76	/**
77	 * Durable record of one delegated attempt. It is what the cell session states
78	 * about an implementer that produced no model-visible history of its own.
79	 */
80	export interface EnvironmentDelegation {
81	  /** One-based attempt this child run implemented. */
82	  readonly attempt: number
83	  /**
84	   * Whether this attempt's prompt restated the task statement ahead of the
85	   * validation directive. A child holds no transcript of the earlier attempts,
86	   * so every attempt after the first restates the task; `false` on the first
87	   * attempt, whose prompt is the task statement alone. It is what tells a
88	   * reader that a later child was given the work and not only the complaint.
89	   */
90	  readonly restatedTask: boolean
91	  /** Subagent provider that ran the child. */
92	  readonly provider: string
93	  /** Parent-scoped id of the child run; the child's session id for an in-process provider. */
94	  readonly runId: SessionId
95	  /** How the child run ended. */
96	  readonly stopReason: EnvironmentDelegationStopReason
97	  /** Structured result the child returned, absent when it returned none. */
98	  readonly structured?: unknown
99	  /**
100	   * Model usage of an in-process child's own session, summed over its
101	   * assistant messages. Absent for a child this process cannot account for,
102	   * which is every out-of-process provider: its tokens are spent in another
103	   * product and never reach a log here.
104	   */
105	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage
106	  /**
107	   * The model the child's own backend stated it ran, as that backend names it —
108	   * an in-process child's route model, an external product's full model id.
109	   * Absent when the provider reports none or the run ended before it did.
110	   * Against the requested model on the `environment/run` stamp it is what
111	   * decides whether a delegated measurement is labelled with the model that
112	   * produced it.
113	   */
114	  readonly reportedModel?: string
115	  /**
116	   * Token accounting the child's own backend reported for the run. It is the
117	   * only spend record an out-of-process child leaves, whose tokens are spent in
118	   * another product; {@link usage} covers an in-process one instead, so at most
119	   * one of the two is stated. Absent when the provider reported none.
120	   */
121	  readonly reportedUsage?: TokenUsage
122	  /**
123	   * Cost in US dollars as the child's own backend priced the run. It is a
124	   * foreign product's accounting rather than a harness pricing table, so it is
125	   * comparable across attempts of the same implementer and never summed with a
126	   * `usage/priced` cost. Absent when the provider reported none.
127	   */
128	  readonly reportedCostUsd?: number
129	}
130	
131	/**
132	 * One rung of an attempt ladder: what the attempt at that index runs on, and
133	 * how much of the run's budget it may spend getting there.
134	 */
135	export interface EnvironmentRunRung {
136	  /**
137	   * Model route this attempt runs on; absent runs the run's own
138	   * {@link EnvironmentRunRequest.model}. A delegated attempt is started on the
139	   * rung's `model` id alone, because a provider names its own models; the
140	   * rung's `provider` is the harness route the same rung names and is what the
141	   * stamp records either way.
142	   */
143	  readonly model?: EnvironmentRunModel
144	  /**
145	   * Fraction of every cap the cell runs under — tokens, wall clock, and cost —
146	   * this attempt may consume before it is ended and the run moves to the next
147	   * rung, greater than 0 and at most 1. It is measured from the cell's caps
148	   * rather than from what is left of them, so a cheap first rung cannot spend
149	   * the budget a later rung was given. Absent lets the attempt run until the
150	   * cell's own caps end it, which ends the cell with it. A ladder whose shares
151	   * sum above 1, and a share outside the range, are refused before any agent
152	   * exists, as is any share in a composition with no budget policy to take a
153	   * share of.
154	   */
155	  readonly share?: number
156	}
157	
158	/** One request to run a registered environment as one fresh session. */
159	export interface EnvironmentRunRequest {
160	  /** Registered environment to run. */
161	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
162	  /** Existing absolute directory the session is rooted at; the task fixture is overlaid onto it. */
163	  readonly workspace: string
164	  /** Model route for this run; absent uses the composition's default model selection. */
165	  readonly model?: EnvironmentRunModel
166	  /**
167	   * One rung per attempt, in attempt order: attempt `i` runs on
168	   * `ladder[i - 1].model`, or on {@link model} for a rung that names none, and
169	   * spends at most `ladder[i - 1].share` of the cell's caps. Present, the
170	   * ladder's length is this run's attempt bound and overrides the composition's
171	   * `maxAttempts`, because the caller that chose a model per attempt is the
172	   * caller that chose how many attempts there are. An empty ladder, one longer
173	   * than the deployment's configured rung ceiling, and one whose shares are
174	   * unusable are refused before any agent exists. Absent runs every attempt on
175	   * {@link model} under the configured `maxAttempts`.
176	   */
177	  readonly ladder?: readonly EnvironmentRunRung[]
178	  /**
179	   * Who does the work of each attempt; absent runs the session's own model
180	   * route. A delegated run is validated identically: only the way the
181	   * workspace reaches its next state changes.
182	   */
183	  readonly implementer?: EnvironmentRunImplementer
184	  /** Zero-based repetition of this environment inside its batch; absent means `0`. */
185	  readonly repetition?: number

193	   * not version.
194	   */
195	  readonly policyVersion?: string
196	  /**
197	   * Sampling seed every request of the run asks for, a safe non-negative
198	   * integer written into the stamp; absent leaves the composition's own
199	   * sampling in place.
200	   */
201	  readonly seed?: number
202	  /** Aborts the implementer's turns and the check commands when it fires. */
203	  readonly signal?: AbortSignal
204	}

206	/**
207	 * One attempt: the implementer's turn followed by one run of the current

211	export interface EnvironmentRunAttempt {
212	  /** One-based attempt number. */
213	  readonly attempt: number
214	  /**
215	   * Model route this attempt ran on: its ladder rung, or the run's stamped

232	/** Outcome of one environment run, returned after the session is flushed. */
233	export interface EnvironmentRunReport {

235	  readonly environment: EnvironmentId
236	  /** Session the run created; its log is the durable record. */
237	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
238	  /** The `environment/run` stamp the session log carries, exactly as appended. */

241	  readonly attempts: readonly EnvironmentRunAttempt[]

244	  /** Certificate of the passing run, present exactly when `certified` is `true`. */

253	  readonly usage?: TokenUsage

255	   * The caps this cell ran under, in cap evaluation order, as

17	/**

20	 * omits the field and one that spells `{ kind: 'route' }` out are one
21	 * experiment and freeze to one digest.

24	  /**
25	   * Who does the work of every cell of this arm — the arm's own model route,

34	   * no model or exactly the arm's `provider` and `model`, and a plan whose
35	   * first rung names another route is refused, because the arm the result is
36	   * published under would not be the arm the first attempt ran. Each rung's
37	   * budget share is frozen into the digest with its route, so two arms that
38	   * divide one cell budget differently are two experiments. Absent runs every

50	  /** Resamples drawn per bootstrap interval. */
51	  readonly bootstrapResamples: number

53	  readonly confidenceLevel: number
54	  /** Certificate-rate delta the overall interval's lower bound must exceed to promote. */

67	  readonly environments: readonly EnvironmentId[]

69	  readonly repetitions: number

204	   * reader of a stored result never has to find the composition that produced

1	/**
2	 * Freezing one experiment plan: the content digest computed before any cell
3	 * runs, and the stamp `group` each arm's sessions carry so a later fold can
4	 * find them in the logs.
5	 *
6	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-experiments/plan
7	 */
8	
9	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
10	import type { BudgetCap } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-budget-policy'
11	import type { EnvironmentRunImplementer, EnvironmentRunRung } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-environment-runner/types'
12	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
13	import type { ExperimentArmPlan, ExperimentArmRole, ExperimentPlan, ExperimentThresholds } from './types.ts'
14	
15	/**
16	 * Group namespace this package owns. A `group` starting with it names an
17	 * experiment arm, so no other producer may mint one.
18	 */
19	export const EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX = 'experiment-'
20	
21	/** Self-declared version of the digested plan fields; a change to what they cover changes it. */
22	const EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION = 6
23	
24	/** Arm roles in the order the digest and the runs take them. */
25	export const EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES: readonly ExperimentArmRole[] = ['baseline', 'candidate']
26	
27	const GROUP_PATTERN = new RegExp(`^${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}([0-9a-f]{64})-(${EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.join('|')})$`)
28	
29	/**
30	 * The implementer one arm runs under.
31	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
32	 * @returns the named implementer, or the arm's own model route when it names none.
33	 */
34	export function armImplementer(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): EnvironmentRunImplementer {
35	  return arm.implementer ?? { kind: 'route' }
36	}
37	
38	/**
39	 * One implementer as the digest takes it: the discriminant, the subagent
40	 * provider, and its label, each in a fixed position, so the key order a caller
41	 * happened to write cannot change the digest.
42	 */
43	function digestedImplementer(implementer: EnvironmentRunImplementer): readonly (string | null)[] {
44	  switch (implementer.kind) {
45	    case 'route':
46	      return [implementer.kind, null, null]
47	    case 'subagent':
48	      return [implementer.kind, implementer.provider, implementer.label ?? null]
49	    /* v8 ignore next 2 -- EnvironmentRunImplementer is closed and every member is handled above */
50	    default:
51	      return assertNever(implementer, 'arm implementer')
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/** One rung as the digest takes it: its model route, then its budget share, each in a fixed position. */
56	type DigestedRung = readonly (readonly string[] | number | null)[]
57	
58	/**
59	 * One arm's attempt ladder as the digest takes it: the model and budget share
60	 * of each rung in attempt order, with `null` for a rung that names no model and
61	 * therefore runs the arm's own route, and `null` for a rung claiming no share
62	 * and therefore running until the cell's own caps end it. Two arms that ladder
63	 * differently, or that divide one cell budget differently, measure different
64	 * routing, so both are part of what the digest freezes.
65	 */
66	function digestedLadder(ladder: readonly EnvironmentRunRung[] | undefined): readonly DigestedRung[] | null {
67	  if (ladder === undefined) return null
68	  return ladder.map(rung => [
69	    rung.model === undefined ? null : [rung.model.provider, rung.model.model],
70	    rung.share ?? null,
71	  ])
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Whether one arm's first rung names a route other than the arm's own. The arm
76	 * is what a result and every scoreboard row are published under, so a first
77	 * rung naming another route would publish the arm's identity over an attempt it
78	 * never ran.
79	 * @param arm - one arm as the plan names it.
80	 * @returns `true` when the arm ladders and its first rung names another route.
81	 */
82	export function ladderConflicts(arm: ExperimentArmPlan): boolean {
83	  const first = arm.ladder?.[0]?.model
84	  if (first === undefined) return false
85	  return first.provider !== arm.provider || first.model !== arm.model
86	}
87	
88	/**
89	 * Content digest of the fields that decide what an experiment measures: the
90	 * two arms in role order, each with its model route, its attempt ladder with
91	 * the budget share of every rung, and its implementer, the environment ids
92	 * sorted so a caller's listing order cannot change the identity, the repetition
93	 * count, the policy version and base seed both arms ran under, the thresholds,
94	 * and the caps every cell of both arms ran under.
95	 * The caps are digested because a cell cut off at one wall or token ceiling
96	 * measures something different from the same cell cut off at another, so two
97	 * comparisons run under different budgets are two experiments, and the shares
98	 * are digested for the same reason one rung down. The deployment's
99	 * token budget stays absent: it bounds what a deployment pays for across plans,
100	 * not what one comparison measures. The policy version and the seed are present
101	 * because both arms' sessions are found in the logs by the groups this digest
102	 * mints, so two comparisons that differ in either must not collide on one group.
103	 * @param plan - the arms, environments, repetitions, policy version, and seed to freeze.
104	 * @param thresholds - the resolved statistical choices to freeze with them.
105	 * @param caps - the caps both arms resolve to, in cap evaluation order.
106	 * @returns the SHA-256 hex digest; identical inputs give identical digests.
107	 */
108	export function planDigest(
109	  plan: ExperimentPlan,
110	  thresholds: ExperimentThresholds,
111	  caps: readonly BudgetCap[],
112	): string {
113	  const content = JSON.stringify({
114	    version: EXPERIMENT_PLAN_VERSION,
115	    arms: EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.map(role => [
116	      role,
117	      plan[role].provider,
118	      plan[role].model,
119	      digestedImplementer(armImplementer(plan[role])),
120	      digestedLadder(plan[role].ladder),
121	    ]),
122	    environments: [...plan.environments].sort(),
123	    repetitions: plan.repetitions,
124	    policyVersion: plan.policyVersion ?? null,
125	    seed: plan.seed ?? null,
126	    thresholds: [
127	      thresholds.bootstrapResamples,
128	      thresholds.confidenceLevel,
129	      thresholds.minimumDelta,
130	      thresholds.cellTokenCap,
131	    ],
132	    caps,
133	  })
134	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
135	}
136	
137	/**
138	 * Whether two arms would run their cells under the same ceilings.
139	 * @param baseline - caps resolved for the baseline arm, in cap evaluation order.
140	 * @param candidate - caps resolved for the candidate arm, in the same order.
141	 * @returns `true` when both lists name the same caps at the same values.
142	 */
143	export function capsAgree(baseline: readonly BudgetCap[], candidate: readonly BudgetCap[]): boolean {
144	  return baseline.length === candidate.length
145	    && baseline.every(([cap, limit], index) => {
146	      // The length check above makes every index of `baseline` an index of
147	      // `candidate`, which the element type does not say.
148	      const [otherCap, otherLimit] = candidate[index] as BudgetCap
149	      return otherCap === cap && otherLimit === limit
150	    })
151	}
152	
153	/**
154	 * Render one arm's caps for a diagnostic.
155	 * @param caps - the caps to render, in cap evaluation order.
156	 * @returns `cap=limit` pairs separated by commas, or `none` for an uncapped arm.
157	 */
158	export function describeCaps(caps: readonly BudgetCap[]): string {
159	  return caps.length === 0 ? 'none' : caps.map(([cap, limit]) => `${cap}=${limit}`).join(', ')
160	}
161	
162	/**
163	 * Stamp `group` one arm's sessions carry.
164	 * @param digest - the frozen plan digest.
165	 * @param role - which arm the group names.
166	 * @returns `experiment-<digest>-<role>`.
167	 */
168	export function experimentGroup(digest: string, role: ExperimentArmRole): string {
169	  return `${EXPERIMENT_GROUP_PREFIX}${digest}-${role}`
170	}
171	
172	/**
173	 * Read a group minted by {@link experimentGroup}.
174	 * @param group - a stamp group from an `environment/run` event.
175	 * @returns the digest and role, or `undefined` for a group outside this package's namespace or malformed inside it.
176	 */
177	export function parseExperimentGroup(group: string): { digest: string; role: ExperimentArmRole } | undefined {
178	  const match = GROUP_PATTERN.exec(group)
179	  if (match === null) return undefined
180	  return { digest: match[1] as string, role: match[2] as ExperimentArmRole }
181	}
182	
183	/**
184	 * Tokens a plan may spend at its per-cell cap: every environment, every
185	 * repetition, on both arms.
186	 * @param plan - the environments and repetitions to project.
187	 * @param cellTokenCap - tokens one cell may spend.
188	 * @returns the projected ceiling the token budget is checked against.
189	 */
190	export function projectedTokens(plan: ExperimentPlan, cellTokenCap: number): number {
191	  return plan.environments.length * plan.repetitions * EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES.length * cellTokenCap
192	}

143	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {

148	  /**
149	   * Freeze a plan, run both arms through the fleet at the same repetition
150	   * indexes, and fold the paired comparison. The arms run as one paired fleet
151	   * run whose cells alternate, so neither arm is confounded with the hour it
152	   * ran in. Every refusal happens before the first cell runs; a cell the fleet
153	   * kept as an error leaves its repetition unpaired instead of failing the
154	   * experiment.
155	   * @param plan - environments, repetitions, the two arms with their model
156	   *   routes and optional attempt ladders and implementers, the workspace root,
157	   *   and an optional policy version, base seed, frozen digest, abort signal,
158	   *   and result sink.
159	   * @returns the digest, both arms with their ladders and stamp groups, one
160	   *   cell per environment, every cell an arm kept as an error, the pooled
161	   *   delta with its interval, the spend, the caps both arms ran under, and
162	   *   the verdict.
163	   * @throws {@link ExperimentError} for a plan that names no or a duplicate or
164	   *   unregistered environment, asks for no repetition, sets a seed that is not
165	   *   a safe non-negative integer, carries an arm ladder with no rung or one
166	   *   whose first rung names another route, whose two arms would run under
167	   *   different caps, declares a digest its content does not freeze to, or
168	   *   projects more tokens than the budget.
169	   * @throws {@link EnvironmentRunError} unchanged from
170	   *   {@link EnvironmentRunner.checkImplementer}, when either arm names an
171	   *   implementer provider this composition cannot honor.
172	   */
173	  async run(plan: ExperimentPlan): Promise<ExperimentResult> {
174	    const { digest, caps } = this.freeze(plan)
175	    const arms: ExperimentArms = {
176	      baseline: resolveArm(plan.baseline, digest, 'baseline'),
177	      candidate: resolveArm(plan.candidate, digest, 'candidate'),
178	    }
179	    const [baseline, candidate] = await this.ctx.fleet.runPaired(armPlan(plan, arms.baseline), armPlan(plan, arms.candidate))
180	    const result = foldExperiment({
181	      digest,
182	      arms,
183	      environments: plan.environments,
184	      repetitions: plan.repetitions,
185	      thresholds: this.resolved.thresholds,
186	      caps,
187	      baseline,
188	      candidate,
189	    })
190	    await record(result, plan.sink)
191	    return result
192	  }
193	
194	  /**
195	   * Validate the plan and both arms' implementers, resolve the caps both arms
196	   * run under, compute the digest over them, and check the projection against
197	   * the budget.
198	   */
199	  private freeze(plan: ExperimentPlan): { digest: string; caps: readonly BudgetCap[] } {
200	    if (!Number.isInteger(plan.repetitions) || plan.repetitions < 1) {
201	      throw new ExperimentError(`repetitions must be a positive integer, got ${String(plan.repetitions)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
202	    }
203	    if (plan.seed !== undefined && !isSeed(plan.seed)) {
204	      throw new ExperimentError(`seed must be a non-negative integer, got ${String(plan.seed)}`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
205	    }
206	    if (plan.environments.length === 0) throw new ExperimentError('the plan names no environment', 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
207	    for (const role of EXPERIMENT_ARM_ROLES) {
208	      const arm = plan[role]
209	      if (arm.ladder?.length === 0) {
210	        throw new ExperimentError(`the ${role} arm's attempt ladder names no rung`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
211	      }
212	      if (ladderConflicts(arm)) {
213	        const first = arm.ladder?.[0]?.model as EnvironmentRunModel
214	        throw new ExperimentError(`the ${role} arm runs ${arm.provider}/${arm.model} but its first ladder rung names ${first.provider}/${first.model}, so its first attempt would not be the arm it is published under`, 'EXPERIMENT_LADDER_CONFLICT')
215	      }
216	      // Both arms are checked here, so an implementer this composition cannot
217	      // honor refuses the plan rather than failing every cell of the arm that
218	      // names it — which, for a candidate arm, would spend the baseline arm in
219	      // full first and then fold to `inconclusive` with nothing paired. The
220	      // arm's own route is the stamped one: a first rung naming another route
221	      // was refused above.
222	      this.ctx.environmentRuns.checkImplementer(armImplementer(arm), { provider: arm.provider, model: arm.model })
223	    }
224	    const named = new Set<EnvironmentId>()
225	    for (const environment of plan.environments) {
226	      if (named.has(environment)) throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is named twice`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
227	      if (this.ctx.environments.get(environment) === undefined) {
228	        throw new ExperimentError(`environment "${environment}" is not registered`, 'EXPERIMENT_INVALID_PLAN')
229	      }
230	      named.add(environment)
231	    }
232	    const caps = this.agreedCaps(plan)
233	    const digest = planDigest(plan, this.resolved.thresholds, caps)
234	    if (plan.digest !== undefined && plan.digest !== digest) {
235	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan declares digest ${plan.digest} but freezes to ${digest}`, 'EXPERIMENT_PLAN_NOT_FROZEN')
236	    }
237	    const projected = projectedTokens(plan, this.resolved.thresholds.cellTokenCap)
238	    if (projected > this.resolved.tokenBudget) {
239	      throw new ExperimentError(`the plan projects ${projected} tokens over a budget of ${this.resolved.tokenBudget}`, 'EXPERIMENT_OVER_BUDGET')
240	    }
241	    return { digest, caps }
242	  }
243	
244	  /**
245	   * The caps both arms run their cells under. A comparison whose arms stop at
246	   * different ceilings measures the ceilings as much as the arms, so the plan is
247	   * refused before either arm starts rather than reported with a caveat.
248	   * @param plan - the frozen plan, supplying the implementer of each arm.
249	   * @returns the caps every cell of both arms runs under, in cap evaluation order.
250	   * @throws {@link ExperimentError} when the two arms resolve to different caps.
251	   */
252	  private agreedCaps(plan: ExperimentPlan): readonly BudgetCap[] {
253	    const baseline = this.ctx.environmentRuns.cellCaps(armImplementer(plan.baseline))
254	    const candidate = this.ctx.environmentRuns.cellCaps(armImplementer(plan.candidate))
255	    if (!capsAgree(baseline, candidate)) {
256	      throw new ExperimentError(`the arms would run under different caps — baseline ${describeCaps(baseline)}, candidate ${describeCaps(candidate)} — so their cells would not be comparable`, 'EXPERIMENT_UNEQUAL_CAPS')
257	    }
258	    return baseline
259	  }
260	}

122	function cellError(error: unknown): FleetCellError {
123	  if (error instanceof HarnessError) return { code: error.code, message: error.message }
124	  return { message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }

127	/** Run `tasks` in task order with at most `limit` in flight. */
128	async function bounded(tasks: readonly (() => Promise<void>)[], limit: number): Promise<void> {
129	  let next = 0
130	  const worker = async (): Promise<void> => {
131	    while (next < tasks.length) {
132	      const index = next
133	      next += 1
134	      await (tasks[index] as () => Promise<void>)()
135	    }
136	  }
137	  await Promise.all(Array.from({ length: Math.min(limit, tasks.length) }, worker))
138	}

145	/**
146	 * Running state of one plan: the consecutive errors each model route has
147	 * produced and the spend the reported cells have folded. Both are read as a
148	 * cell is about to start, so a refusal only ever keeps an unstarted cell out of
149	 * the runner and never interrupts one in flight.
150	 */
151	class PlanLedger {
152	  private readonly consecutiveErrors = new Map<string, number>()
153	  private inputTokens = 0
154	  private outputTokens = 0
155	
156	  constructor(
157	    private readonly breaker: RouteBreakerConfig | undefined,
158	    private readonly ceiling: number | undefined,
159	  ) {}
160	
161	  /** Model usage of every cell folded so far. */
162	  get spend(): FleetSpend {
163	    return { inputTokens: this.inputTokens, outputTokens: this.outputTokens }
164	  }
165	
166	  /**
167	   * The refusal that keeps a cell out of the runner.
168	   * @param cell - the cell about to start.
169	   * @returns the error to record for the cell, or `undefined` when nothing refuses it.
170	   */
171	  refusal(cell: FleetCell): FleetCellError | undefined {
172	    const spent = this.inputTokens + this.outputTokens
173	    if (this.ceiling !== undefined && spent >= this.ceiling) {
174	      return {
175	        code: 'FLEET_TOKEN_CEILING_REACHED' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
176	        message: `the plan's token ceiling of ${this.ceiling} was reached at ${spent} tokens`,
177	      }
178	    }
179	    const errors = this.consecutiveErrors.get(routeName(cell.model)) ?? 0
180	    if (this.breaker !== undefined && errors >= this.breaker.consecutiveErrors) {
181	      return {
182	        code: 'FLEET_ROUTE_BREAKER_OPEN' satisfies FleetCellErrorCode,
183	        message: `route ${routeName(cell.model)} stopped after ${errors} consecutive errors`,
184	      }
185	    }
186	    return undefined
187	  }
188	
189	  /**
190	   * Fold one outcome the runner produced. A refused cell never reaches this,
191	   * so a refusal neither opens another route's breaker nor moves the spend.
192	   * @param outcome - the settled outcome of one cell the runner handled.
193	   */
194	  record(outcome: FleetCellOutcome): void {
195	    const route = routeName(outcome.cell.model)
196	    if ('error' in outcome) {
197	      this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, (this.consecutiveErrors.get(route) ?? 0) + 1)
198	      return
199	    }
200	    this.consecutiveErrors.set(route, 0)
201	    this.inputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0
202	    this.outputTokens += outcome.report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0
203	  }
204	}

206	/** Key of the leaderboard row a cell belongs to. */

211	/**
212	 * Keep the enumerated cells a plan named, in plan order.
213	 * @throws {@link FleetError} when the selection is empty or names a cell the
214	 *   plan's environments, routes, and repetition count do not enumerate.
215	 */
216	function restrict(enumerated: readonly FleetCell[], selected: readonly FleetCell[]): FleetCell[] {
217	  if (selected.length === 0) throw new FleetError('the plan names no cell to run', 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
218	  const wanted = new Set(selected.map(fleetCellKey))
219	  const kept = enumerated.filter(cell => wanted.has(fleetCellKey(cell)))
220	  for (const key of kept.map(fleetCellKey)) wanted.delete(key)
221	  const unenumerated = [...wanted]
222	  if (unenumerated.length > 0) {
223	    throw new FleetError(`cell "${unenumerated[0] as string}" is not one this plan enumerates`, 'FLEET_INVALID_PLAN')
224	  }
225	  return kept
226	}

230	 * same unit of the same plan, so a driver indexing cells across processes —
231	 * against a ledger or against the run stamps already in the session logs —
232	 * keys them by this instead of comparing the records field by field.
233	 * @param cell - the cell to name.

240	/** Fold the leaderboard from the cell outcomes, one row per model route and environment. */
241	function foldLeaderboard(
242	  outcomes: readonly FleetCellOutcome[],
243	  definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>,
244	): LeaderboardRow[] {
245	  const rows = new Map<string, LeaderboardRow>()
246	  for (const outcome of outcomes) {
247	    const key = rowKey(outcome.cell)
248	    const definition = definitions.get(outcome.cell.environment) as EnvironmentDefinition
249	    const row = rows.get(key) ?? {
250	      provider: outcome.cell.model.provider,
251	      model: outcome.cell.model.model,
252	      environmentId: outcome.cell.environment,
253	      environmentKind: definition.kind,
254	      heldOut: definition.heldOut,
255	      runs: 0,
256	      errors: 0,
257	      certified: 0,
258	      certificateRate: 0,
259	      attemptsMean: 0,
260	      inputTokens: 0,
261	      outputTokens: 0,
262	    }
263	    rows.set(key, 'report' in outcome ? withReport(row, outcome.report) : { ...row, errors: row.errors + 1 })
264	  }
265	  return [...rows.values()]
266	}

268	/** Add one report to a row, recomputing the derived rates. */
269	function withReport(row: LeaderboardRow, report: EnvironmentRunReport): LeaderboardRow {
270	  const runs = row.runs + 1
271	  const certified = row.certified + (report.certified ? 1 : 0)
272	  const attempts = row.attemptsMean * row.runs + report.attempts.length
273	  return {
274	    ...row,
275	    ...report.stamp.ladder === undefined ? {} : { ladder: report.stamp.ladder },
276	    isolation: report.stamp.isolation,
277	    implementer: report.stamp.implementer ?? ROUTE_IMPLEMENTER,
278	    runs,
279	    certified,
280	    certificateRate: certified / runs,
281	    attemptsMean: attempts / runs,
282	    inputTokens: row.inputTokens + (report.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0),
283	    outputTokens: row.outputTokens + (report.usage?.outputTokens ?? 0),
284	  }
285	}

287	/**
288	 * One plan prepared to run: what its validation resolved, the cells it
289	 * enumerates in plan order, the ledger those cells fold into, and the slot each
290	 * cell's outcome lands in. A single run and a paired run both fill the slots and
291	 * read the report off this record, so a plan interleaved with another still
292	 * reports what it reports alone.
293	 */
294	interface PlanRun {
295	  readonly plan: FleetPlan
296	  readonly group: string
297	  readonly definitions: ReadonlyMap<EnvironmentId, EnvironmentDefinition>
298	  readonly cells: readonly FleetCell[]
299	  readonly ledger: PlanLedger
300	  /** Each cell's outcome, at that cell's index in {@link PlanRun.cells}. */
301	  readonly outcomes: FleetCellOutcome[]
302	}

304	/** Fold one prepared plan's report, once every cell of it has settled. */
305	function planReport(run: PlanRun): FleetRunReport {
306	  return {
307	    group: run.group,
308	    cells: run.outcomes,
309	    leaderboard: foldLeaderboard(run.outcomes, run.definitions),
310	    spend: run.ledger.spend,
311	  }

314	/** One cell awaiting the pool: the prepared plan that owns it and its index in that plan's cell order. */
315	interface ScheduledCell {
316	  readonly run: PlanRun
317	  readonly index: number
318	}
